- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for risk aversion or market panic.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply a “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 10–20% in the following 2–3 periods.
- If model consistently forecasts below true price with no sentiment signal, consider mean reversion: adjust forecast upward by 1–3% if price has been trending downward for 3+ days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 3% from model in 3+ consecutive days, apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” — blend model with sentiment-adjusted baseline (e.g., 70% model + 30% sentiment trend).
- If sentiment drops sharply after a price spike, model often fails to correct — apply “sentiment lag correction”: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods until sentiment stabilizes.
